newsitem.title: USA: Trial of white cop in black motorist's death opens.
newsitem.headline: Trial of white cop in black motorist's death opens.

text.p: The trial of John Vojtas, one of three white police officers charged with involuntary manslaughter in the suffocation death of a black motorist, opened Monday before an all-white jury.

The death of Jonny Gammage, a 31-year-old cousin and business partner of Pittsburgh Steelers defensive lineman Ray Seals, has drawn national attention because of its racial overtones. Gammage died last year on a roadside while in the custody of five white police officers.

The trial for the other officers charged in the case, Brentwood Lt. Milton Mulholland and Baldwin Patrolman Michael Albert, ended in a mistrial last month. A new trial is to take place next year. Vojtas' trial is expected to last two weeks.

"I hope (Vojtas' trial) moves swiftly and with dispatch," said Esther Bush, president of the Urban League of Pittsbugh. "I hope everyone involved is careful enough to do the appropriate thing in the name of justice."
Gammage died in the early morning of Oct. 12, 1995, after a scuffle with the five officers on a roadside in Overbrook, a Pittsburgh suburb. Two policemen were not charged.

According to the officers' testimony at a coroner's inquest following the incident, Gammage was driving erratically, prompting Mulholland to pull him over. Gammage became violent after leaving his car while the other four officers were arriving at the scene, they said.

The officers said Gammage was so violent they had to restrain him by holding him on the ground. Allegheny County Coroner Cyril Wecht, who was hired by the Gammage family to review the case, said Gammage died at the scene from suffocation caused by compression to the chest.
The jury for Vojtas' trial was chosen from Lackawanna County in northeast Pennsylvania because of pre-trial publicity. The jury consists of seven men and five women.
